claims.statement: The HO-6 2014-04 form is effective April 1, 2014 and is superseded by HO-6 2023-02 for policies effective on or after February 1, 2023, while remaining applicable to policies written under the earlier edition; HO-6 2023-02 is effective February 1, 2023.

HO 04 35 expressly applies only while attached and controls conflicting policy language; HO 04 91 has its own coverage, exclusions, limit, and deductible provisions and applies only while it is in effect, but its preamble does not state the same conflict-control rule as HO 04 35.

HO-6 separates unit-owner property coverages A through D from Section I Additional Coverages and Section II liability coverages E and F; Section II Coverage E is Personal Liability and Section II Coverage F is Medical Payments to Others.

Under HO-6 2014-04, Coverage A covers unit building items and certain exclusively used or commonly owned property only to the extent of the insured's ownership interest or legal responsibility, has a default $5,000 limit, and applies an 80% Coverage A replacement-cost threshold only when the damaged property is repaired or replaced as required by the policy; the threshold does not change the amount of insurance provided.

Under HO-6 2023-02, Coverage A covers unit building property, attached fixtures and components, improvements, materials, and property the unit owner is required to insure by governing documents or law; it has a default $10,000 limit, retains the 80% replacement-cost threshold, excludes detached structures from Coverage A, and does not cover association-responsibility property absent an obligation to repair or replace it.

Coverage B is separate from the unit-building layer: both editions use a set-apart or limited-connection test and a residential-use boundary; 2014-04 separately addresses structures under construction, materials, temporary removal, garages, storage, recreation, and certain structures rented with the dwelling, while 2023-02 expressly excludes structures rented or held for rental to another person and structures used for business; attached structures fall outside the Other Structures boundary.

Both HO-6 editions provide worldwide Coverage C personal-property treatment, but 2023-02 raises the stated special limits for money, jewelry, firearms, watercraft, business property, and electronic apparatus over the 2014-04 amounts while leaving the silverware limit at $2,500; these limits remain within Coverage C.

Both editions set Coverage D at 50% of the Coverage A limit and cover qualifying additional living expense, fair rental value, and civil-authority loss of use; 2023-02 expressly requires notice when the premises becomes uninhabitable and habitable, limits payment after access is restored, and requires reasonable efforts concerning existing rental arrangements.

HO-6 2014-04 lists named property perils and separately excludes flood, surface water, subsurface water, sewer or drain backup, sump overflow, earth movement, gradual seepage, defective conditions, pollutants, and intentional loss; HO-6 2023-02 retains the named-peril structure and adds detailed boundaries for water, vacancy, theft, collapse, roof surfacing, cosmetic damage, and utility failures.

Both HO-6 editions require prompt notice, protection and preservation of damaged property, inspection access, records, cooperation, and recovery-right preservation; both state a $500 minimum Section I deductible, require a sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request, and provide payment within 60 days after agreement on the covered loss.

Section II Coverage E in both editions pays legally owed damages for bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense for a covered suit; 2023-02 states a more granular exclusion set than 2014-04, including business, rental, care-custody-control, communicable-disease, abuse, cyber or data, water, and animal risks.

Section II Coverage F is no-fault Medical Payments to Others coverage for qualifying third-party injury; the editions cover injury on an insured location and specified off-premises pathways, and 2023-02 expressly measures medical expenses within three years after the accident.

Attached HO 04 35 modifies loss-assessment treatment: its 2014-04 edition covers an insured's share of covered association property-loss or liability assessments up to $10,000, while its 2023-02 edition covers collective-property loss, a covered master-policy deductible, or covered association liability up to $25,000 and excludes ordinary maintenance, betterment, fines, business, contractual, and speculative assessments.

The HO-6 base form's loss-assessment additional coverage is $1,000 in 2014-04 and $2,000 in 2023-02, so those base limits must be distinguished from the higher HO 04 35 limit when that endorsement is attached.

HO 04 91 writes back unit-owner coverage for direct physical loss caused by sewer or drain backup and sump overflow or discharge to covered building and personal property, while preserving exclusions for flood, surface water, groundwater, gradual leakage, and repair of the failed system; it supplies a $7,500 limit, but its deductible section contains a drafting anomaly that states $750 as a maximum payment rather than unambiguously stating a $750 deductible.

HO 17 32 is the repository's 2014-04 unit-owner rental endorsement: its terms apply to an insured unit only while rented to others or held available for rental, cover specified landlord-owned tenant-use property and loss of rent after a covered loss makes the unit unfit, exclude a tenant's personal property merely because it is present, and limit landlord's furnishings to $5,000.

HO-6 2023-02 separately provides $3,000 landlord's-furnishings coverage and fair-rental-value Coverage D language, so the 2014-04 HO 17 32 terms must not be applied to a 2023-02 policy without checking the policy schedule and attached endorsements.

Attached HO 17 33 modifies 2014-04 Coverage A by using a risk-of-direct-physical-loss grant for unit building property and setting a $25,000 Coverage A limit, while preserving its stated exclusions for flood, surface water, groundwater, sewer or sump backup, and other excluded causes.

The 2023-02 HO-6 source contains apparent drafting defects, including repeated wording in the vacancy definition and repeated words in endorsement cross-references, so those phrases should be flagged rather than silently normalized.

The HO-6 filing memorandum explains the 2023-02 revision as clarification of covered-property descriptions, loss settlement, post-loss information and cooperation, water-related causes, loss of use, liability, medical payments, and selected limits; it is explanatory context and does not replace the operative form or an attached endorsement.

HO 04 35 expressly requires attachment, and HO 04 91 applies only while it is in effect; a base-form cross-reference to a water-backup endorsement is not by itself proof that the endorsement was issued with the policy.

HO-6 Coverage A protects the unit owner's covered ownership interest or contractual/legal responsibility for repair or replacement, not the condominium association's entire building as a matter of course; the 2014-04 form limits common-property payment to the insured's interest or responsibility, and the 2023-02 form excludes association-owned or association-responsibility property unless an agreement or governing obligation makes the insured responsible to repair or replace it.

A unit-owner claim should be analyzed in sequence by governing edition, insured property interest, cause or path of loss, exclusions and named-peril boundaries, declarations limits and deductibles, attached line-specific endorsements, and post-loss duties; appraisal addresses amount of loss rather than creating coverage.

The 2023-02 HO-6 source contains apparent drafting defects, including duplicated vacancy-definition wording and malformed repeated endorsement cross-reference text; those defects should be flagged and not silently corrected by importing memorandum or training language.
